items.title: PG&E, Edison Suffer Biggest Stock Drops in Years on California Wildfire Legislation
items.summary: Shares of publicly traded utilities tumbled today after an effort by California Gov. Gavin Newsom to shield the sector from wildfire-related lawsuits was rejected by state lawmakers.  California utility PG&E shares tumbled 20%, their biggest drop since the Covid-19 selloff of March 2020.  Other California-based utility stocks also sank, including Edison International.

items.title: PG&E Stock Is Priced For A Decision It Does Not Make
items.summary: PG&E's cash-flow multiple sits far below the market's, and the company says its capital plan is premised on how California resolves wildfire liability.

items.title: California Utility Stocks Plummet After Wildfire Legislation Announced
items.summary: California utility stocks tanked after Gov. Gavin Newsom and state legislators reached a deal on a bill effectively limiting the liability related to wildfire damages faced by insurers.  S&P 500 stock Edison International sold off 26% and PG&E plummeted 24%, according to MarketSurge.  Meanwhile, Sempra, the holding company that owns San Diego Gas & Electric and Southern California Gas Company, was down about 8%.

items.title: PG&E Stock Plummets as California Withholds Wildfire Liability Protections
items.summary: PG&E stock falls sharply after the California State Assembly amends key wildfire legislation that leaves out liability protection for utilities.
